purpose: the real per-cell cost of emitting one condensed operator, measured, because '2 s per cell' had never been
what_was_quoted: 2 s per cell, a budget set early and never measured against the full-factor decode

measured_2026_09_20.device: RTX 5090, otherwise idle, chunk 8192 (the only verified chunk), min of 3 repeats

cpu_for_contrast.note: measured while four training arms shared the box; 50.8x the GPU

the_two_corrections: AGAINST US: the 2 s budget is MISSED by 2.69x at q = 10812, on an idle GPU, with nothing else running. It is met only at small q. Stop quoting 2 s/cell as achieved; it is achieved at q = 711 (0.026 s) and not at q = 10812.
FOR US: the 273 s CPU figure measured earlier tonight is not the deployment cost either - the GPU is 50.8x faster. Neither number should be quoted alone.

comparison_per_delivered_operator_entry.why_per_entry: their operator is 171 or 14196 independent entries and ours is q(q+1)/2 = 5.85e7, so a wall-clock comparison of 2 s against 19 ms compares objects that differ by 4100x to 342000x in size

huang_eml63_3d.source: EML 63:102041 section 4.3, 1.024e6 substructures, 5677.8 s per optimisation iteration; the 5.5 ms includes assembly, solve and OC, of which OC alone is about 26 %

chen_li_cad193_p3.source: CAD 193 Table 2, 15.6 s / 675 elements and 31.1 s / 1600 elements, 3D elasticity, p = 3, 10^3 local fine mesh, C++/Eigen/TBB on an i7-11700

comparison_per_delivered_operator_entry.reading: per delivered entry we are 15-350x faster than the measured classical cost, while delivering 4100-342000x more entries. 'The classical route is too slow' remains indefensible; 'the classical route does not deliver this object at all' is the defensible form.

open: the 5.37 s materialises the full dense q x q factor. Whether deployment needs it materialised, or only its action, has not been examined - a matrix-free lattice solve would change this number and has never been costed.
